name: Creidne

attributes.attribute: an artisan god of the Tuatha Dé Danann called the brazier
specialized in precious metals, bronze and gold
the three craft gods, with Goibniu and Luchtar
king whose silver hand some tales credit to Creidne

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Creidne counts among the gods of Ireland, an artisan member of the magical Tuatha Dee Danann. His craft title was brazier, his work lying in bronze and gold and other fine metals. With Goibniu and Luchtar he made up the craft of the three deities, the na tree dui Dana. His people's weapons against the Fomorians came from his forge. Some tales name him the maker of the silver hand given to king Nuada on his wounding, a task other versions give to Cian Ceccht. A tale tells that Creidne drowned carrying gold out of Spain. Another figure of the name served among the Warrior Women beside the Fianna.

okr.objective: Creidne is an Irish artisan god of the Tuatha Dé Danann.
key_results: He worked in bronze and gold as one of the three craft gods.
He forged weapons against the Fomorians.
Tales differ on whether he or Dian Cécht made Nuada's silver hand.
Reports of his drowning come from a gold import from Spain.
